checks.current_native_statement: A cellular algebra need not be semisimple, its cell modules need not be simple, and a labelled head $D^{\lambda}$ may vanish although the cell module $C^{\lambda}$ is nonzero. (a) Abstract degenerate instance: let $F$ be a field and $A=F[x]/(x^2)$, with $\Lambda=\{1\rhd2\}$ ordered so that $1\rhd2$, cellular basis $c_{11}:=1$ in cell $1$ and $c_{22}:=x$ in cell $2$ and $i=\mathrm{id}$ ([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]). The triangular axiom holds because $1\cdot a\equiv0\bmod(x)$ for $a\in(x)$ and $x\cdot a\in\{x,0\}$, and $A^{\rhd2}=0$. The cell form on $C^{2}$ has $c_{22}c_{22}=x^2=0$, so it is identically zero, $\mathrm{rad}\,C^{2}=C^{2}$ and $D^{2}=0$, while $C^{1}\cong F$ is simple: cellularity does not force $D^{\lambda}\ne0$, and the algebra is not semisimple since $\mathrm{rad}\,A=(x)$. (b) Hecke instance: let $F$ be a field of characteristic $2$ and $q=1$, so $e=\operatorname{char}(F)=2$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]); for $n=3$ and $\lambda=(1,1,1)$ the partition $(1,1,1)$ is not $2$-regular ([[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]]), so $D^{(1,1,1)}=0$ while the page's Specht module $S^{(1,1,1)}\cong D^{(3)}$ is the nonzero trivial module (in characteristic $2$ the sign module is trivial) ([[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]], [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]). (c) Reducible cell module: at $e=2$ the q-Schur cell module $W^{(3,2)}_F$ satisfies $\sum_{i>0}[W^{(3,2)}_F(i)]=[L^{(3,1^2)}_F]+2[L^{(2^2,1)}_F]\ne0$ ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]], the calculation of [[ex-q-schaper-for-shape-three-two-at-e-two]]), so its radical is nonzero and $W^{(3,2)}_F$ is reducible even though it has a simple head.

Then for all partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ the modules $S^{\lambda}$ and $S^{\mu}$ lie in the same block of $H_{F,q}(S_n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). (For $e=\infty$ the Hecke algebra is semisimple and each partition is its own core, so the statement is the trivial block decomposition.)
